name: formula-scan
desc: Free, open-source math OCR for Windows — photos of formulas and handwriting to LaTeX offline. 100 MB portable, MIT, no page limits.
features: ✅ **Formula to LaTeX** — photograph an equation and get editable LaTeX in the clipboard
✅ **Handwritten support** — lecture notes and whiteboard scribbles recognized, not just printed print
✅ **Live render preview** — see the typeset formula beside the photo to catch recognition mistakes
✅ **Batch pages** — a folder of note photos converted into one .tex document with page separators
✅ **MathML and plain-text output** — for Word, web and script consumers, not just LaTeX users
✅ **Correction pass** — nudge individual symbols the model got wrong with a symbol keyboard
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, models download separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Paid per month | Paid | Your time |
| Unmetered use | **Yes** | Snip limits | License | N/A
| Photos stay local | **Yes** | Upload | Yes | N/A
| Batch pages to one .tex | **Yes** | Partial | Partial | Manual
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | App and web | Installer | N/A
faqQ: convert photos of math formulas to LaTeX offline and for free?
faqA: Mathpix is good and charges monthly with uploads, and hand-typing equations is the most expensive option of all. formula-scan recognizes printed and handwritten math locally, previews the typeset result and exports LaTeX or MathML. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, no page limits.
s1: Dark recognizer (#121418, green #22C55E): photo of a handwritten integral left, rendered LaTeX right in matching layout, confidence chip at 0.96.
s2: Correction pass: symbol grid under the formula with two items highlighted amber, symbol keyboard panel below, apply button enabled.
s3: Batch pages: 34 note photos listed with recognition status, single .tex output checkbox checked, progress bar at 22 of 34, format dropdown reading LaTeX.
